# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 73 (Bu-Vb Sk73)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk73
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 73
**Title (English, from literature):** Defecating while standing
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The rule regulates bodily deportment, specifying that a monk should neither defecate nor urinate while standing unless he is sick [Dhammika, Broken Buddha]. Modern Vinaya discussions highlight interpretive questions regarding the application of the illness exception in contemporary settings, such as using public urinals when private cubicles are occupied [Dhammika, Broken Buddha]. An English translation of the rule is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
